tickets.title: GitHub OAuth login + Redis sessions
acceptance: GitHub OAuth authorization-code flow per FR-AUTH-1 (docs/SRS.md §2.7): first login creates a user row linked to GitHub id/login/avatar; E2E against a mocked GitHub completes the round-trip to an authenticated session
Sessions per FR-AUTH-2: httpOnly+secure cookie, server-side Redis store, idle timeout + absolute lifetime, logout revokes; expired session yields 401 with the docs/API_DESIGN.md §1 error envelope
Endpoints match the docs/API_DESIGN.md §2 'auth' catalog
notes: HANDOFF for W1-04: authRoutes (apps/api/src/routes/auth) is fastify-plugin-wrapped, so registering it once at the top level in app.ts (app.register(authRoutes, {...})) makes request.session available app-wide — do not also separately register the session plugin from @repopulse/auth, it is already composed in. GET /me currently returns only {user} (id/forgeUserId/login/name/avatarUrl/createdAt) — workspace/role/identity_id/default_view_id per API_DESIGN.md #2 need the workspace/RBAC infra this ticket owns (packages/auth/src/workspace/**); extend /me rather than replace it. Routes are mounted at their literal catalog paths (/auth/login, /auth/callback, /auth/logout, /me), not prefixed under /api/v1 — matches "every route (except /auth/*, /webhooks/*, /healthz) requires a session" treating /auth/* as a peer namespace to /api/v1, not nested under it; flag if that reading turns out wrong.

Real architectural gap (surfaced via AskUserQuestion before building): FR-AUTH-1 identity fetch needs GET api.github.com/user, which trips validate-arch.sh rule 4 (no api.github.com outside packages/forge) but packages/auth cannot depend on packages/forge (dependency matrix runs forge -> auth, not the reverse). User chose a narrow, grepped, documented rule-4 exception for packages/auth/src/oauth/** over inverting the dependency direction. Documented in SECURITY_CONTROLS.md SC-12/AC-4 (this base URL is a fixed literal using the user's own OAuth token, never admin/attacker-supplied input, so the SSRF-allowlist threat model does not apply). Verified the exception stays narrow by deliberately violating rule 4 in an unrelated file first and confirming the validator still failed it.

Scope-completion widenings (same class as W1-01's tsconfig.json/package.json gap, not new scope creep): packages/shared/src/index.ts never re-exported the db/** module W1-01 built (package main pointed at the placeholder barrel only) -- fixed since every future consumer of @repopulse/shared needs it, not just this ticket. .env.example gained API_BASE_URL (apps/api's own origin for the OAuth redirect_uri; PUBLIC_BASE_URL is the SPA on a different origin, and no var existed for the API's own URL). package.json dependency additions verified against real node_modules/registry (Law 2) before use: @fastify/cookie, @fastify/session, ioredis, fastify-plugin, drizzle-orm, @repopulse/shared (as an explicit dep of packages/auth and apps/api, both needed it directly), dotenv (test-only, matching drizzle.config.ts's existing convention for loading .env in scripts outside the app runtime).

Idle timeout + absolute lifetime (FR-AUTH-2) both verified against installed library source, not assumed: @fastify/session 11.1.2's default rolling:true re-derives cookie.originalMaxAge on every request and calls store.set() every response, so the hand-written RedisSessionStore applies that as the Redis key's PX TTL on every set() -- sliding idle timeout for free. Absolute lifetime has no library equivalent; enforced independently by stamping session.createdAt once at login and rejecting in store.get() once exceeded, regardless of the Redis TTL still being live -- covered directly by a live-Redis unit test (packages/auth/src/session/redis-store.test.ts) that sets a long idle TTL but a stale createdAt and confirms get() still returns null.

Closed 2026-07-16: full gate green -- lint/typecheck/test (16 test files/26 tests, up from 13/13), validate-arch (rule 4 exception verified narrow), validate-plan, validate-traceability, validate-compose, validate-egress-audit all pass. E2E against a real mocked-GitHub HTTP server (not a fixture) walks the full login -> callback -> /me -> logout -> /me-401 round trip plus state-mismatch/missing-cookie rejection, using the live compose Postgres + Redis (scripts/dev-up.sh) -- migrations applied fresh, test data cleaned up in afterAll (verified zero leftover user rows / Redis keys post-run).

tickets.title: Workspaces, roles and /api/v1 skeleton (error envelope, OpenAPI, authZ hooks)
acceptance: Fastify /api/v1 skeleton with error envelope {code,message,requestId}, OpenAPI generated from route schemas, and the shared cursor/sort/window/repo-set list-param fragment per docs/API_DESIGN.md §1 (FR-API-1/3/4)
Every route requires a session and is workspace-scoped; launch ships single 'default' workspace with auto-membership on first login (FR-AUTH-3, FOUNDING_BRIEF D1)
Role enforcement admin vs member per FR-AUTH-4: a member calling any admin (crown) route in docs/API_DESIGN.md §2 receives 403 — matrix test over all admin routes
notes: Error envelope reconciliation: ticket text and SRS FR-API-4 say the envelope is {code,message,requestId}, but API_DESIGN.md §4 ("canonical shapes — copy these exactly") is authoritative and gives RFC 7807 {type,title,status,detail,instance,request_id} — which W1-03 already shipped on the wire. Concluded {code,message,requestId} (also in DASHBOARD.md §3) describes the frontend web client's own surfaced error state after parsing this response, not a second wire format apps/api must also emit. Built the shared apps/api/src/plugins/error-envelope.ts + lib/problem.ts to the §4 shape; did not touch apps/api/src/routes/auth/problem.ts (W1-03's ticket-local duplicate of the same shape) since it's outside this ticket's write_scope — functionally correct as-is, just duplicated code; flagged for whoever next touches routes/auth to migrate onto the shared helper.

First-member-becomes-admin (FR-AUTH-3 auto-membership): undocumented in SRS/UX_SPEC/FOUNDING_BRIEF. Decided the first member of the default workspace is admin, everyone after is member — required for bootstrap (an admin route is otherwise permanently unreachable) and matches UX_SPEC's "Connect your org (admin) / Ask an admin" empty-state copy assuming the setup user is admin. ensureMembership's count-then-insert has a narrow race window between two concurrent first-ever logins (both could read zero members and both insert as admin) — accepted for launch scale: failure mode is a redundant second admin, not a privilege escalation, not worth an advisory lock for this skeleton ticket.

Real Fastify preHandler bug found via testing (not assumed): an async preHandler that calls reply.send() (via sendProblem) and then implicitly returns undefined does not reliably short-circuit Fastify's remaining preHandler chain when more than one preHandler applies to a route (apiV1's plugin-level addHook preHandler + a route's own preHandler option, e.g. requireAdmin). Manifested as a second, overlapping onSend/session-save cycle and an unhandled ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT rejection — caught by the synthetic-route RBAC test (api-v1.test.ts), reproduced 100% deterministically, root-caused via targeted debug instrumentation (not guessed), fixed by explicitly `return reply` on every early-exit preHandler path in both requireAdmin (lib/rbac.ts) and apiV1's own guard (plugins/api-v1.ts). Worth flagging for any future preHandler that short-circuits via reply.send() alongside other preHandlers on the same route.

RBAC "matrix test over all admin routes" acceptance criterion: zero real admin (crown) routes exist yet — connections/admin catalog sections are all later-wave feature tickets with no backing infra. Built the reusable requireAdmin gate + proved it against a synthetic route registered inside apiV1's own encapsulated scope exactly how a real feature-route ticket is meant to extend it (documented in api-v1.ts's HANDOFF comment), rather than adding placeholder admin routes to app.ts (would misrepresent what's actually built). Real admin routes inherit the same guard automatically once registered as children of apiV1.

Retry policy per §3: secondary 403/429 honors retry-after, else x-ratelimit-reset, else >=60s exponential backoff; 5xx retried 3x jittered; instrumentation counters/gauges from §3 exposed (NFR-12)
notes: Branched off main directly, not the still-unmerged W1-04 PR, since W1-05 only depends_on W1-01 and its write_scope (packages/forge/src/{types,provider}.ts, client/**) is disjoint from W1-04's files.

Transport-agnostic design (the key scope decision): BudgetedClient takes an injected RequestExecutor rather than depending on @octokit/* directly, even though those packages are already pinned in TECH_STACK.md. This means the same class serves both GitHubProvider (W1-06, Octokit-backed executor) and the future Gitea adapter (W7-02, fetch-backed executor) against FORGE_PROVIDER.md §5's shared contract-test suite, and lets all four acceptance-criteria tests run against a mock executor with zero real HTTP. Octokit composition (throttling plugin as a secondary safety net on top of whichever executor W1-06 builds) is explicitly deferred to that ticket.

SC-12 SSRF allowlist scope split: SECURITY_CONTROLS.md says this control "ships in W1 ... so the GT ticket [W1-06] inherits, not reinvents" and "Lands: W1 · packages/forge" - but it is in neither W1-05's nor W1-06's own 4 acceptance criteria. Rather than skip it (the doc clearly intends it lands somewhere in W1/packages/forge) or build the full thing speculatively, split it: the string-level half that needs no network resolution (https-only, exact-match hostname allowlist, reject bare IPv4/IPv6 literals and disguised decimal/octal/hex-encoded IPs, reject localhost/*.localhost) is built here as client/base-url.ts with the canonical evil-URL corpus as unit tests. The "resolve-then-pin the IP" DNS-rebinding defense needs actual socket-level control that only a concrete transport has - left for whichever executor W1-06/W7-02 construct, flagged here and in STATUS.md so it isn't silently dropped.

NFR-12 instrumentation: no metrics-exposition library (e.g. prom-client) is pinned anywhere in the repo. Built ForgeMetrics as an in-memory counters/gauges/histogram registry exposed via BudgetedClient.metricsSnapshot() rather than pulling in a new dependency unilaterally - a future ops ticket (E9.3, GET /admin/budget, DEPLOYMENT.md §7 GET /metrics) is expected to read this snapshot and render it in Prometheus format.

Budget-floor semantics (FR-INGEST-4 cross-check): BudgetedClient.request() denies outright (throws ForgeBudgetParkedError) when the primary bucket is at/below the floor for backfill/reconcile lanes - it does NOT internally queue-and-wait for a reset (resets can be up to an hour away). This matches FR-INGEST-4's "each BullMQ job draws from the budget and yields when the floor is hit, rescheduling itself" - the job-level retry loop is ingest's responsibility, not the client's. Separately, ConcurrencyQueue DOES do real in-process async queuing with lane-priority ordering, but only for the <=100 concurrent-slot semaphore (FORGE_PROVIDER.md §3's "PriorityQueue" stage) - slot waits are always short (another in-flight call finishing), unlike budget-floor waits.

Endpoint-key bug caught before commit: an early draft computed the ETag cache key once for the lookup (including the URL's query string) but recomputed it differently (without the query string) at store()-time, which would have silently broken the cache for every parameterized request. Caught by re-reading my own diff before running tests, not by a failing test; fixed by computing the key once per request() call and threading it through to the retry loop.

Case-insensitive header parsing bug caught by its own test: parseGithubRateLimitHeaders' header lookup only tried the exact key and the fully-lowercased key, so a header arriving as e.g. "X-RateLimit-Remaining" (mixed case, possible from a non-normalizing executor even though real fetch/undici always lowercase) silently returned undefined. Fixed to scan all header keys case-insensitively; kept the defense even though the comment notes real executors normalize case, since BudgetedClient's executor is an arbitrary injected function, not guaranteed to.

Fixed a stale doc reference while in TECH_STACK.md: the Octokit section said the budgeter "wraps Octokit" and persists ETags to an "api_cache" table - neither was ever true (no api_cache table exists anywhere in packages/shared's schema; forge_etag is the real, only table) - corrected to describe the transport-agnostic design.

tickets.title: Tenancy isolation test suite (route walker, two-workspace fixture)
acceptance: Two-workspace fixture; a route walker asserts every registered /api/v1 route returns zero cross-workspace rows (NFR-4, FR-AUTH-3); adding an unscoped route fails the walker
Suite runs inside pnpm test and is part of the full gate from W1 on (MASTER_PROMPT §Hard rules: tenancy invariant)
notes: trackRoutes(app) attaches Fastify's onRoute hook. Verified empirically (not assumed): app.register(plugin) only queues the plugin via avvio, actual route registration happens during the boot sequence triggered by app.ready()/listen()/first inject() - so attaching onRoute AFTER all app.register() calls but BEFORE app.ready() still captures every nested/encapsulated plugin's routes. This means no change to apps/api/src/app.ts's buildApp() was needed; the walker is a pure test-time addition.

walkForTenancyLeakage is generic and route-shape-agnostic: it does a plain substring search for each OTHER probe's marker string in the raw response body, not a schema-aware check. This means it needs zero per-route knowledge and will automatically start covering real feature routes (repos/PRs/findings/etc.) as later-wave tickets add them, with no changes to this suite required.

Real structural finding (not guessed): v1 ships a single 'default' workspace (D1) and ensureMembership (W1-04) hardcodes that slug - there is no way today for two different real login sessions to resolve to two different real workspaces; multi-tenant resolution doesn't exist yet by design (NFR-4 explicitly frames this as "D1 SaaS-ready", i.e. proving readiness ahead of need). Rather than stub request.workspace directly (which would test nothing about the real preHandler chain), the live test uses one real login (resolves to 'default' via the real session->workspace->role preHandler, same as production) plus a second workspace row inserted directly as data (never resolved through any session) whose name is a unique marker string. This proves the walker against real DB/session/preHandler machinery, not a synthetic harness.

Acceptance criterion "adding an unscoped route fails the walker" demonstrated two ways: (1) packages/shared/src/testing/route-walker.test.ts - a fully synthetic, DB-free unit test with a fabricated scoped-vs-unscoped route pair, proving the walker mechanism in isolation; (2) apps/api/test/tenancy/route-walker.test.ts - the same property against the REAL apiV1 guard/session/DB: a 'scoped-ok' route (WHERE id = request.workspace.id) passes with zero violations, a deliberately-unscoped 'scoped-bad' route (no filter, returns every workspace row) is caught by name.

Parameterized routes (containing ':') are explicitly skipped by the walker - none exist yet among real /api/v1 routes (all future-wave feature tickets), and synthesizing a valid path for an arbitrary parameterized route needs per-route fixture data the walker can't infer generically. Documented as a known future extension point, not silently ignored.

Scope-completion widening: packages/shared/src/testing/** needs Fastify's FastifyInstance/InjectOptions types, so 'fastify' was added to packages/shared/package.json as an OPTIONAL peer + dev dependency (matching packages/auth's precedent of taking a framework peer dep without becoming a framework package) - packages that never import the testing barrel (metrics/analysis/insights/reports) aren't forced to install it. Re-exported ./testing/index.js from packages/shared/src/index.ts alongside the existing ./db/index.js re-export (same barrel-completeness pattern as the W1-01/W1-03 gaps found earlier).

tickets.title: Badge tint fails WCAG AA in BOTH themes — measured, systemic
acceptance: Every SeverityBadge and HealthBadge variant reaches >=4.5:1 measured against the ACTUAL rendered background (the /15 tint over --color-surface), in dark AND light, not against --color-bg
An axe scan of a populated route (org overview with seeded data) passes with zero color-contrast violations — add it to e2e as a standing assertion
theme.css comment updated: the AA claim states which background the check was run against
notes: Found 2026-08-12 by the W4-03 axe run on real data — jsdom component tests cannot compute contrast, so this survived W4-02 green. MEASURED, all on the /15 tint the badges actually use (blend alpha 0.15 of the token over the surface beneath it): DARK over --color-surface #161b22 — sev-critical/health-attend #f85149 = 4.35 FAIL, sev-high #db6d28 = 4.27 FAIL, sev-info #8b949e = 4.50 borderline, sev-medium 5.37 ok, sev-low 5.31 ok, health-good 5.32 ok. LIGHT over --color-surface #f6f8fa — EVERY token fails: sev-critical #cf222e 3.97, sev-high #bc4c00 3.84, sev-medium #9a6700 3.77, sev-low #0969da 3.97, sev-info #656d76 4.07, health-good #1a7f37 3.92. The pattern is the defect, not the palette: tinting the background with the SAME hue as the text eats the contrast, and theme.css line 18 claims -AA-checked >=4.5:1 text- because it was checked against --color-bg, where the dark values do pass (4.73-6.02). Candidates verified for dark if the /15 pattern is kept: #ff7b72 = 5.44 (Primer dark red), #f0883e = 5.40. Light theme likely needs a neutral tint rather than a same-hue one. This is a design-system call (tokens vs tint pattern), which is why it is not folded into W4-03.

DONE 2026-08-12. Fixed by MEASURING the alternatives rather than picking colours. Measured every candidate at alphas 0/0.08/0.10/0.15 over BOTH card surfaces in BOTH themes, which settled the design question: at alpha 0 every existing token already passes (light min 4.57, dark min 5.13), so the PALETTE was never the defect — the same-hue /15 tint was. No single alpha works for both themes (dark tolerates 0.10, light fails at any tint because its tokens are AA against WHITE and the card surface leaves no headroom), and a neutral surface-2 chip still left three light tokens failing (4.29-4.48). So the tint pattern is kept — least visual change — and 12 tokens moved to the palettes own darker/brighter Primer steps: dark sev-critical/health-attend #f85149→#ff7b72, sev-high #db6d28→#f0883e, sev-info #8b949e→#b1bac4; light sev-critical/health-attend #cf222e→#a40e26, sev-high #bc4c00→#953800, sev-medium/health-watch #9a6700→#7d4e00, sev-low #0969da→#0550ae, sev-info #656d76→#424a53, health-good #1a7f37→#116329. Worst case after: 4.94 (dark) / 5.03 (light) on a /15 tint over surface-2 — headroom, not a squeak past. theme.css now STATES which background the AA claim was checked against, since the old blanket -AA-checked >=4.5:1- against --color-bg is exactly what hid this.

STANDING ASSERTION added as e2e/a11y.spec.ts — axe on a POPULATED route in BOTH themes, which is the gap that let this ship: the shell smoke scans an UNAUTHENTICATED page where the API 401s and no badge ever renders, and the web component tests run in jsdom, which cannot compute contrast at all. Light is only reachable via the theme toggle, so a dark-only scan would have kept missing the worse theme (6 failing tokens vs 2). BOTH scans RED-checked by restoring the old value: dark #f85149 and light #cf222e each fail their own spec with color-contrast, then restored. ALSO FIXED a flake I introduced in the W4-13 spec: .count() and .allInnerTexts() are one-shot reads, and each sparkline is its own /metrics/series query resolving AFTER the KPI row paints, so it failed ~1 run in 3. Swapped to retrying expect(locator) assertions and tightened to toHaveCount(5) — one sparkline per tile, which also catches a single tile silently losing its series. Five consecutive clean runs; RED re-verified after the refactor. Gate: lint clean, typecheck clean, test 462/462, e2e 9/9.

tickets.title: Seeder fixture cannot satisfy the org screens: single-point series, one window bucket, absolute dates
acceptance: Each metric gets a multi-point series per repo AND at org level (repo_id NULL) — at least enough points that a sparkline renders (>=2) and a trend delta has a prior value to compare against
Snapshots exist for every window preset the UI offers (7d/30d/90d/365d), not only the 30d bucket
Commits/PRs/snapshots are anchored RELATIVE to run time, so the DEFAULT window always contains fixture data whenever the suite runs
Determinism preserved: re-seeding still produces identical values via the seeded RNG (existing determinism/idempotence tests stay green)
An e2e assertion covers the DEFAULT window and asserts KPI VALUES (not em dashes) plus a rendered sparkline — the assertion W4-03 could not write
notes: Found 2026-08-12 while writing the W4-03 e2e. Seeded commits span 2026-06-01..2026-06-24 as ABSOLUTE dates, but the suite ran on 2026-08-12 — so the default 30d window contains ZERO commits and /hotspots returns {items:[]}, rendering the leaderboard empty state instead of data. W4-03 specs work around it by asserting at window=90d, which is honest for -renders from the warehouse- but leaves the default path untested. This is a time bomb, not a one-off: once the fixture is >365d old EVERY window preset goes empty and every W4-W6 screen e2e silently degrades to asserting empty states. Fix the anchoring before more screen tickets build assertions on top of it.

DIAGNOSIS SHARPENED 2026-08-12 after building W4-03 against the real fixture. Three distinct fixture gaps, all in seed.ts, each independently blocking part of W4-03 acceptance 2: (1) SINGLE-POINT SERIES — the snapshot loop writes exactly one row per (repo|org) x metric at one computedAt, so every series has length 1. KpiRow renders no sparkline below 2 points (deliberately: a 1-point line reads as -no change- rather than -no history-), so sparklines can NEVER render, at any window. (2) ONE WINDOW BUCKET — every row is written with window=30d, so /org/summary?window=90d finds nothing and all five tiles render em dashes. Verified: select window, count(*) → 30d | 48, org rows 12. (3) ABSOLUTE DATES — commits span 2026-06-01..06-24, so on 2026-08-12 a 30d window has zero churn and /hotspots returns {items:[]}. Net effect: KPIs need window=30d, hotspots need 90d, sparklines need a series that does not exist — NO single window satisfies acceptance 2, which is why W4-03 is blocked on this rather than working around it.

DONE 2026-08-12. All three fixture gaps fixed in packages/shared/src/testing/seed/seed.ts. (1) ANCHORING: the absolute BASE=2026-06-01 is replaced by anchorFor(now) — UTC-midnight-quantised, SPAN_DAYS=40 back from today, injectable via opts.now. Quantising to midnight is what preserves determinism: two seeds on the same UTC day produce identical timestamps, so the existing determinism/idempotence tests stay green unchanged. Commit spacing widened c*3→c*5 and PR spacing p*4→p*7 so activity reaches the recent end of the span instead of bunching in the first three weeks. (2) SERIES: snapshots are now a weekly walk of SERIES_POINTS=8 per (scope x metric x window) instead of one point — a clamped random walk per series so deltas are non-zero and each tile moves independently rather than in lockstep. (3) WINDOWS: written for all four presets (7d/30d/90d/365d), not just 30d. Counts 48 → 1536 rows (12 metrics x 4 scopes x 4 windows x 8 points); the one-row-at-a-time insert became a 500-row batched insert, and seeding got FASTER (seeder tests 713ms, ~3x). BOTH new e2e assertions RED-checked rather than assumed: SERIES_POINTS=1 fails exactly -KPI sparklines should render-, and dropping the 30d bucket fails exactly -first KPI tile should carry a real value at the default window-; each restored after. Screen now renders 5 valued tiles with deltas, 5 sparklines and 9 hotspot rows at the DEFAULT window. Gate: lint clean, typecheck clean, test 462/462, e2e 7/7.

Built apps/api/src/routes/views/{schema,serializer,cursor,share-slug,index}.ts: GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /views (cursor-paginated, owner-scoped list — see judgment call below), POST /views/{id}/share, GET /views/shared/{slug}, PUT /me/default-view. Judgment calls (documented per Bug Fix / Code Quality discipline, not silently guessed): (1) GET /views lists only the caller's OWN views, not workspace-wide "shared with me" — API_DESIGN.md's endpoint row doesn't specify, and FR-WEB-4's "switcher in nav" reads as a personal list; shared access is exclusively via GET /views/shared/{slug} per FR-WEB-5. Real bug found and fixed (verified empirically via a standalone tsx repro before touching test code, not assumed): calling reply.send() (via sendProblem) from inside an async route HANDLER after a prior await, then resolving with undefined, causes @fastify/session's onSend hook to run a second time (a second Session.save()/store.set() racing the first), throwing ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT ~500ms later — reproduced outside vitest with a minimal script, confirmed via redis-store.ts instrumentation that store.set() fired twice for one request. Same failure class as W1-04's documented requireAdmin/api-v1.ts preHandler fix, but manifesting in a terminal route handler rather than a chained preHandler. Fixed by adding a local fail() helper (sendProblem + explicit return reply) and converting all 17 early-return call sites; instrumentation reverted, confirmed via git diff clean on redis-store.ts.

DONE and VERIFIED RUNNING: a single multi-stage Dockerfile with four targets (api, worker, migrate, web) sharing one dependency + build stage so a full compose build resolves the pnpm workspace once; deploy/compose.yaml with nothing bpmforge-specific in it; deploy/nginx.conf.template; deploy/.env.example where every secret is blank with its generation command; docs/INSTALL.md. Node pinned to 22.23.1 and pnpm to 9.15.9, matching .nvmrc and packageManager — a container silently running a different Node major is the NODE_MODULE_VERSION failure the test-on-stop hook documents.

BUILT AND SMOKE-TESTED FOR REAL, not just written. Three bugs found by running it, each of which would have hit a customer on their first `up`: (1) REDIS EXITED 127 — cap_drop:[ALL] removes CAP_SETUID/SETGID, so the image entrypoint could not drop privileges and died with only a `setpriv: setresuid failed` line to explain itself; fixed with `user: redis`. (2) REDIS REPORTED UNHEALTHY FOREVER — the healthcheck used $REDIS_PASSWORD but the password was only substituted into `command`, never into the container environment, so redis-cli ran unauthenticated; api/worker/web all have depends_on: service_healthy and therefore sat in Created indefinitely. A stack that starts nothing, with a healthy-looking redis. (3) NGINX EXITED ON BOOT — proxy_pass resolves upstreams at STARTUP and hard-fails on an unknown host, so the web container died before the API existed; now templated through ${API_UPSTREAM} via the nginx template mechanism, which also lets one image point at an API that is not a sibling container.

Migrations ran to completion against the compose Postgres before api/worker started, and a second `up` is a no-op. Port isolation confirmed by inspection, not assumption: postgres, redis, api and worker publish NO host ports; only web does, bound to 127.0.0.1 so nothing is exposed before the operator puts TLS in front.
